language.title: Language
language.intro: Changes apply immediately and are remembered on this device.
language.label: Display language
language.contribute: Applyer is translated by its community. A language missing or wrong? Corrections are welcome on the project's issue tracker.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.intro: Choose which job events should send a desktop notification when Applyer is in the background or hidden.
notifications.enabledHint: Allow Applyer to send notifications through your operating system.
notifications.verificationRequiredHint: A CAPTCHA or another verification challenge needs your attention.
notifications.permissionRequiredHint: An agent is waiting for approval to complete fields or upload a document.
notifications.jobFilledHint: An application has been filled and is ready for you to review and submit.
notifications.jobFailedHint: A queued or in-progress job could not be completed.
notifications.testFailed: Could not send the test notification.

search.title: Job search
search.intro: Most job sites are one site per country, each with its own listings: a search on the US edition of Indeed never sees a job posted to the Australian one, and Seek only exists in Australia and New Zealand. Pick where you are looking so every search goes to the right edition. The agent can still search another country for a single query when you ask it to.
search.outro: Company boards you track (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday) are searched regardless of country.
search.saved: Job searches will use the {{country}} editions.
search.saveFailed: Could not save the job search country.
search.challengeFallback: When a site refuses a headless search, open it in the application browser and ask me to clear its verification challenge
search.challengeFallbackHint: Some sites (Prosple, for one) answer Applyer's hidden browser with a challenge no matter what and clear the same page in a visible window within seconds. With this on, a search that gets refused opens the page in the application browser (or your attached browser) and a banner asks you to look at it; with it off, the site is reported as blocked and the other sites carry on.
search.challengeFallbackSaved: Refused searches will open in the application browser.
search.challengeFallbackOff: Refused searches will be reported as blocked.

sources.indeed: General job board with a separate edition and index per country.
sources.linkedin: One worldwide site; narrowed by the location you give the search, not by country.
sources.seek: The main job board in Australia and New Zealand.
sources.jora: Worldwide aggregator that re-lists postings from other boards and career pages. Copies of jobs found elsewhere are dropped.
sources.prosple: Graduate programs, internships and entry-level roles across Asia-Pacific.
sources.remotive: Remote-only roles, worldwide, read through its public API.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.intro: Changes apply immediately and are remembered on this device.
appearance.terminalNote: Terminal tab: the terminal itself updates immediately, but a CLI agent already running inside it (Codex, Claude, etc.) only detects light/dark once at startup. Restart it after changing the theme if it looks off.
appearance.canvasTintHint: Shifts the hue of panels, borders, and backgrounds while keeping their contrast unchanged.
appearance.cssIntro: Injected live into the app as you type. It can only change how things look, not how they work. If it ever makes the UI unusable, press <1>{{shortcut}}</1> anywhere to clear it instantly.
appearance.deletePresetMessage: This deletes the preset "{{name}}". The custom CSS editor keeps its current contents; this can't be undone.
appearance.loadPresetMessage: This overwrites what's currently in the custom CSS editor with the selected preset.
appearance.replaceMessage: This overwrites what's currently in the custom CSS editor with the selected template.
appearance.clearMessage: This removes all custom CSS you've written. This can't be undone.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.intro: Every shortcut requires holding {{modifier}}, except function keys (F1-F24, which don't produce typed characters). Plain typing, including inside the terminal, is never intercepted.
shortcuts.conflictMessage_one: {{combo}} is currently bound to "{{commands}}". Setting it here removes it from that command.
shortcuts.conflictMessage_other: {{combo}} is currently bound to "{{commands}}". Setting it here removes it from those commands.
shortcuts.resetAllMessage: This restores every shortcut to its default binding, discarding any customization.

browser.intro: Applyer drives a Chromium-based browser to search and apply to jobs. By default it looks for your system's installed Chrome or Edge first, and only downloads its own copy if neither is found.
browser.devBuildNote: This is a development build, so it always uses Playwright's bundled Chromium regardless of the preference below. The preference only takes effect in a packaged build.
browser.unresolvedNote: Resolves the first time a browser is needed, e.g. searching or applying to a job.
browser.outro: Auto tries system Chrome, then Edge, then a one-time managed download. Picking Chrome or Edge specifically fails with an error (instead of silently trying something else) if that browser isn't installed. Managed download always uses Applyer's own downloaded copy.
browser.saved: Browser preference saved. It takes effect the next time a browser is launched.
browser.saveFailed: Could not save the browser preference.
browser.allowLocalAddressesHint: Developer option for testing sites on localhost or a private network. Off by default.
browser.localAddressesConfirmTitle: Allow access to your local network?
browser.localAddressesConfirmMessage: Agents and job pages will be able to connect to localhost, private IP addresses, and services on your local network. A malicious page could probe or send requests to those services. Only enable this while testing sites you trust.
browser.localAddressesSaved: Local address permission saved. It applies to new browser sessions.
browser.localAddressesSaveFailed: Could not save the local address permission.
browser.remoteIntro: Instead of opening its own window, Applyer can open application forms as new tabs in a browser you already have running, signed in to everything you are signed in to. Nothing is copied or decrypted from that browser's profile.
browser.remoteEnableHint: Applies to the interactive application window only, and overrides the preferred browser above for it (in development builds too). Job searches keep running in Applyer's own headless browser.
browser.remoteEndpointHint: Where the browser listens for DevTools connections. Chrome's default is http://127.0.0.1:9222; Applyer reads the browser's current websocket path from its profile folder itself. For a browser using a custom profile folder, paste the ws:// address from that folder's DevToolsActivePort file instead.
browser.remoteEndpointEmpty: Enter the address the browser is listening on.
browser.remoteEndpointInvalidUrl: That does not look like a valid URL.
browser.remoteEndpointUnsupportedProtocol: The address must start with http://, https://, ws:// or wss://.
browser.remoteTestNoProfile: Reached {{version}}, but it has no profile to attach to. Start it normally, with a window open.
browser.remoteTestWaiting: Waiting for the browser. If it asks whether to allow remote debugging, accept it in the browser window.
browser.remoteHowTo: In Chrome 144 or newer, open chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging and turn on "Allow remote debugging for this browser instance". Chrome asks for your permission when Applyer first connects, then Applyer keeps that connection for the rest of its run. Older browsers need this startup flag instead:
browser.remoteSaved: Browser attachment settings saved. They take effect the next time an application window is opened.
browser.remoteSaveFailed: Could not save the browser attachment settings.
browser.remoteScopeWarning: Remote debugging exposes the entire browser, and every account signed in to it, to any program on this computer that connects to the port, not only Applyer. Turn it off in the browser when you are not using it. Whether it avoids a site's automation detection is not guaranteed either: some detect the debugging connection itself.
browser.remoteConfirmMessage: With remote debugging on, any program on this computer that connects to that port gets full read and control access to the browser and everything you are signed in to, not just Applyer. Applyer's own tools only inspect and fill application forms, but the browser does not enforce that. Only enable this on a computer you trust, and turn remote debugging off in the browser when you are done.

storage.intro: Everything stays on this computer either way. This changes how all stored data is kept on disk, including the database, documents, screenshots, and logs.
storage.encryptedDescription: The complete database and every stored file are encrypted with a key protected by this computer's secure storage. Only readable on this device, by your user account.
storage.plaintextDescription: Stored as regular, readable files. Simpler to back up or inspect, but readable by anyone with access to this computer's files.
storage.encryptionUnavailable: Not available on this system (no OS keychain detected).
storage.changeMessageEncrypted: This will encrypt the complete database, uploaded documents, screenshots, and logs. It may take a moment.
storage.changeMessagePlaintext: This will decrypt the database and stored files into ordinary readable data. It may take a moment.
storage.changed: Storage mode changed. The database and stored files were re-written in the new format.
storage.locationIntro: Where your database, documents, screenshots, and logs are kept. Applyer keeps running while a move is in progress.
storage.moveMessage: Move your database, documents, screenshots, and logs to "{{path}}"? This may take a moment and Applyer will keep running throughout.
storage.connectMessage: Switch to the Applyer database already stored in "{{path}}"? This replaces the currently active dataset with the selected one. Nothing is copied, deleted, or merged, so you can reconnect to the current location later. Applyer will restart automatically.
storage.pickFailed: Could not choose a storage location.
storage.connectFailed: Failed to connect to that storage location.

recovery.title: Your storage location isn't available
recovery.help: Reconnect the drive or folder, then retry. Or use the default location for now: you can switch back once your custom location is available again.
recovery.retryFailed: Could not retry the storage location.
recovery.inspectFailed: Could not inspect the default storage location.
recovery.useDefaultFailed: Failed to switch to the default location.
recovery.confirmMessageEmpty: This uses the default location until you reconnect your custom location and retry, or pick a new one in Settings.
recovery.confirmMessageExisting: The default location already has data in it: {{jobs}} jobs, {{documents}} documents. Using it now continues from that data; it won't merge with your custom location. You can switch back once your custom location is available again.

data.intro: Everything here stays on this computer. Export writes a file you choose, import reads one you pick.
data.exportDescription: Save your job applications, indexed jobs, exclusions, tracked company boards, profile, settings, and appearance to a file, either as one JSON bundle or as a CSV table for spreadsheets.
data.importDescription: Restore data from a JSON file this app exported. New jobs, indexed jobs, exclusions and company boards are added alongside what you already have; profile, settings, and appearance can optionally be overwritten.
data.domainJobsHint: Queued, filled, submitted, and failed jobs on the board.
data.domainIndexedJobsHint: Every posting your searches have surfaced, matched or not. Rows already indexed here are kept as they are.
data.domainExclusionsHint: The blacklist of job URLs to never surface again.
data.domainCompanyBoardsHint: The company job boards searches fetch. Each board arrives unchecked; the next search fills in its role count.
data.domainProfileHint: Your candidate profile fields (uploaded documents are not included).
data.domainResumesHint: The structured master resume and every per-job tailored variant. Variants only import when their job is also present.
data.domainSettingsHint: Auto-start command, notification preferences, and the indexed-jobs retention period.
data.domainThemeHint: Theme mode, accent color, surface tint, and custom CSS (including saved presets). Normally stays on this device only.
data.domainChatsHint: OpenRouter chat sessions and their messages.
data.formatJsonHint: One file bundling everything selected below. This is also the only format Import accepts.
data.formatCsvHint: A flat, spreadsheet-friendly table of a single list. CSV exports cannot be re-imported.
data.importOnlyJson: Only accepts a JSON file previously produced by Export. CSV files cannot be imported.
data.recordsHint_one: {{count}} record in the file. Existing ones (matched by URL) are skipped.
data.recordsHint_other: {{count}} records in the file. Existing ones (matched by URL) are skipped.
data.autoStartReviewWarning: This imported setting will run automatically in every new terminal.
data.autoStartReviewBody: Only continue if you trust the file and have inspected the entire command below. Commands can read, change, upload, or delete files using your account.
data.autoStartReviewAdvice: If anything is unfamiliar, go back and deselect App settings. You can configure a safe command yourself in Settings > Agent.
data.importCompleteEmpty: Import complete. Nothing new to add.
data.resumeAssignmentsLinked_one: {{count}} job linked to its resume variant
data.resumeAssignmentsLinked_other: {{count}} jobs linked to their resume variants
data.resumeAssignmentsUnresolved_one: {{count}} job named a resume variant that does not exist here
data.resumeAssignmentsUnresolved_other: {{count}} jobs named resume variants that do not exist here

agent.autoStartIntro: Automatically type a command into every new terminal session Applyer opens. Handy for dropping straight into an agent CLI so it is ready to use the <1>{{tool}}</1> MCP tools without typing the launch command yourself. Pick a preset, or enter any other command (a different agent CLI, a launcher script, etc). This only affects new sessions.
agent.autoStartSet: The embedded terminal will now auto-run: {{command}}
agent.autoStartCleared: The embedded terminal will open to a plain shell.
agent.connectionsIntro: Applyer exposes tools (search, queue, fill applications, etc.) over MCP. Connect one or more agent CLIs here.

cli.title: CLI agent
cli.description: Type into an embedded terminal running a coding agent CLI you already use.
cli.needs: Needs: an installed agent CLI (Claude Code, Codex, or anything else that speaks MCP).

openrouter.title: OpenRouter
openrouter.description: Chat with an in-app agent that calls the same tools, no terminal or CLI required.
openrouter.needs: Needs: an OpenRouter account with credits.

agent.modeChangeFailed: Could not change the agent mode.

connect.title: OpenRouter connection
connect.browserNote: Your browser should have opened. If it did not, open this link.
connect.pasteLabel: Paste the code or the redirected URL
connect.pastePlaceholder: Paste here if the browser did not redirect back
connect.startFailed: Could not start the OpenRouter connection.
connect.invalidCode: That code or URL was not accepted.
connect.noKeychainBody: This computer has no OS keychain Applyer can use, so the OpenRouter API key would be stored in plain text instead.
connect.allowPlaintext: I understand the key will be stored unencrypted on this computer
connect.disconnectConfirmMessage: Applyer will forget this key. Chat stops working until you connect again.
connect.keyRejectedBody: The key this app holds no longer works: it was deleted on openrouter.ai or has expired. Reconnect to authorize a fresh key; the old one is replaced. Disconnect only removes it.

models.title: Model
models.refreshFailed: Could not refresh the model list.
models.loadFailed: Could not load the model list.
models.staleNote: Showing a cached list from an earlier refresh.
models.selectedMissing: The selected model "{{modelId}}" was not found in the current catalog. It may have been removed.
models.empty: No models are available right now.
models.effortUnsupported: This model does not report support for a reasoning effort.
models.saveFailed: Could not save the OpenRouter settings.
models.toolApprovalIntro: Tick a tool to have the agent ask for your approval in chat before it runs, instead of running immediately.
models.toolApprovalNote: inspect_application, fill_application, and click_application_button also follow the Agent access permissions available in the dock toolbar, regardless of this setting.

mcp.autoConfigureFailed: Auto-configure failed. Use the snippet below instead.
mcp.notConfiguredYet: {{cli}} isn’t configured for {{scope}} yet. Click Auto-configure above, or add the snippet manually, first.

developer.title: Developer settings
developer.intro: Advanced runtime controls intended for development, diagnostics, and unusual installations.
developer.modeHint: Reveals low-level configuration. This does not weaken safeguards by itself.
developer.configurationIntro: Settings are grouped by subsystem. Each saved override is written to settings.json in the app data directory.
developer.restartRequired: Restart Applyer to activate the saved configuration changes.
developer.saved: Setting saved. Restart Applyer to activate it.
developer.resetDone: Setting restored to its default. Restart Applyer to activate it.
developer.jsonHint: Enter a valid JSON array or object.
developer.dangerousMessage: {{setting}} controls a safety, compatibility, or resource limit. An unsuitable value can cause data loss, excessive network usage, or instability.

browserSetup.title: Setting up a browser
browserSetup.confirm: No installed Chrome or Edge was found on this system. Applyer needs a Chromium browser to search and apply to jobs. Download one now? This only happens once.
browserSetup.downloading: Downloading a browser in the background. This is needed for job search and applications.
browserSetup.complete: Browser setup complete. Job automation is ready.
browserSetup.attaching: Attaching to your browser at {{endpoint}}. If it asks whether to allow remote debugging, accept it in the browser window.
